title: Marginal and Conditional Densities
short: f_X(x) = ∫ f(x, y) dy, and X and Y are independent when f(x, y) = f_X(x) f_Y(y) everywhere.
trouble: Students call f(x, y) = 2 on the triangle 0 < x < y < 1 a product of separate functions. Its support is not a rectangle, so X and Y are dependent.

blocks.html: From a joint density we can recover the density of each variable alone and the density of one given the other, just as rows and columns did for joint tables. Sums become integrals.

$$f_X(x) = \int f(x, y)\,dy, \qquad f_{Y \mid X}(y \mid x) = \frac{f(x, y)}{f_X(x)},$$ integrating over the values of $y$ where $f(x, y) > 0$ for that $x$. $X$ and $Y$ are independent when $f(x, y) = f_X(x)\,f_Y(y)$ everywhere, which needs a support that is a rectangle.

$$P(a \le X \le b) = \int_{a}^{b}\left(\int f(x, y)\,dy\right)dx$$ so the inner integral is the density of $X$: integrate out $y$. Dividing a slice $f(x, \cdot)$ by its total $f_X(x)$ makes it a density in $y$, the conditional density. If the support is not a rectangle, some pairs $(x, y)$ are impossible although $x$ and $y$ are each possible alone; there $f(x, y) = 0$ while $f_X(x)f_Y(y) > 0$, so independence fails.

blocks.name: prob-region
blocks.cap: The density 2 on the triangle where x is below y. Each vertical slice runs from y equal to x up to 1, so its total, the marginal density of X, shrinks as x grows.

blocks.title: A constant on a triangle
blocks.q: $f(x, y) = 2$ for $0 \le x \le y \le 1$. Find $f_X$, $f_Y$ and $f_{Y \mid X}(y \mid x)$.
steps: For fixed $x$, $y$ runs from $x$ to 1: $f_X(x) = \int_{x}^{1} 2\,dy = 2(1 - x)$ on $[0, 1]$.
$f_{Y \mid X}(y \mid x) = \frac{2}{2(1 - x)} = \frac{1}{1 - x}$ for $x \le y \le 1$: given $X = x$, $Y$ is uniform on $[x, 1]$.

blocks.title: A sum on the square
blocks.q: $f(x, y) = x + y$ on the unit square. Find $f_X$ and decide whether $X$ and $Y$ are independent.

blocks.title: A product that is not independent
blocks.q: $f(x, y) = 8xy$ for $0 \le x \le y \le 1$. Are $X$ and $Y$ independent?
steps: The formula is a product, but the support is a triangle.
$f_X(x) = \int_{x}^{1} 8xy\,dy = 4x(1 - x^{2})$ and $f_Y(y) = \int_{0}^{y} 8xy\,dx = 4y^{3}$; their product is not $8xy$.

blocks.html: Calling $f(x, y) = 2$ on the triangle $0 < x < y < 1$ "a product of separate functions" because it is constant. The support is not a rectangle, so knowing $X$ limits $Y$ (if $X = 0.9$ then $Y \ge 0.9$). Check two things: the formula splits as (a function of $x$) × (a function of $y$), and the support is a rectangle.
